# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- For media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to work around display restrictions.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- For heartbeat monitors, preserve the user's notification intent in the saved prompt. Unless the user explicitly asks for periodic status updates, instruct the heartbeat to stay quiet while the monitored state is unchanged or non-actionable and to notify only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action. Do not add instructions such as "leave a brief status update" on every run.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_archived`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Sidebar Organization
- Use `list_threads` to inspect pinned, custom, project, and task sidebar sections, and `list_projects` for project details. Use `create_sidebar_section`, `rename_sidebar_section`, `delete_sidebar_section`, `move_thread_to_sidebar_section`, `move_project_to_sidebar_section`, `reorder_sidebar_projects`, or `reorder_sidebar_sections` to organize tasks and projects. Moving an item into the pinned section pins it.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Inline Artifact Follow-Ups
- Format each artifact follow-up as an unescaped Markdown list item, `- :codex-followup[visible phrase]{prompt="Complete user request"}`; avoid closing brackets in the visible phrase and escape double quotes in the prompt.

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.

# AGENTS.md instructions for C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os

<INSTRUCTIONS>
# Global rules — Joshua

These apply on **every** project on this machine, in every session. Project-level
`AGENTS.md` files add to this; they do not replace it.

Keep this file short. It reloads on every message.

---

## Who

Joshua Fisseha — `contact@aspiringattorneys.com`. Builds **LSAT U** (lsatprep.study) and
the Aspiring Attorneys brand. Teaches the LSAT: ~25 one-to-one sessions a week plus
consultations. Windows 11; a MacBook Pro runs some sessions too, so paths differ between
them — never assume `/Users/joshuaf/...` resolves here.

## Where things live

- **AI OS / second brain:** `C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os` — the Obsidian vault. `context/`,
  `wiki/`, `students/`, `corpus/`, `decisions/`, `brainstorms/`, `skills/`, `projects/`.
  Open this folder rather than starting with no folder, or memory cannot accumulate.
- **Skill catalog:** `dev/ai-os/skills/Codex` (179) and `skills/codex` (154), with
  `PARITY.md` declaring deliberate single-runtime skills and `INDEX.md` cataloging them.
- **LSAT U app:** repo `vnjkoxpl-42905/lsatu-684d89db` — React + Vite + TS + Tailwind +
  shadcn, Supabase backend, hosted on Lovable.
- **GitHub:** account `vnjkoxpl-42905` (auto-generated name, correct account).

## How to work with him

- **Do the whole task.** Deliver the finished thing, then say plainly what you skipped
  and why. Don't hand back a plan when the work was asked for.
- **Look before asking.** If the answer is on disk or reachable through a connected tool,
  go get it. He has Firecrawl, Google Workspace (`gws`), and `gh` — use them.
- **Say what's actually true.** Distinguish verified from assumed, every time. If a step
  failed or was skipped, lead with that. A confident wrong answer costs more than "I
  don't know yet."
- **Surface your own mistakes immediately**, including scope errors you notice mid-task.
- Absolute dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`), never "yesterday" or "last week".
- Don't re-ask what he already answered. Don't pad with options he didn't request.

- **Dictation fixes.** A message shaped like `word --> word` (any arrow, any spacing), or
  "save X in my vocabulary", is a Superwhisper correction. Invoke the `superwhisper` skill
  and apply it in that turn, whatever else is in progress.

## Writing as Joshua

Anything published under his name — course copy, lessons, emails, posts.

Plain, direct, confident. Short sentences. Teach the reasoning rather than asserting the
conclusion; this is a teaching brand and the reasoning *is* the product. Concrete beats
abstract. Never condescend to the reader.

**Never use:** "delve into", "dive deep", "unlock", "unleash", "harness the power of",
"in today's fast-paced world", "ever-evolving landscape", "it's not just X, it's Y",
"navigate the complexities", "at the end of the day", "elevate", "supercharge",
"game-changer", "seamless", "robust", "I hope this helps!", "Great question!",
"Certainly!". No em-dash pile-ups. No paragraph opening with "Moreover," /
"Furthermore," / "Additionally,". No emoji in professional writing unless asked.

Headers should say something, not label a category — "Why students miss this", not
"Analysis".

## Safety

- **Draft by default; send only when he says "send".** Email, messages, posts are drafted
  and shown to him. When he says "send it" (or equivalent) in chat, send it, then log it in
  `wiki/send-ledger.md`. Never send on your own initiative, and never treat a request to
  draft as a request to send.
- **Never delete** files, emails, or records without explicit confirmation.
- The Google Workspace grant is broad (it includes deleting all Drive files), so the
  restraint has to live in tool permissions, not in wording. A prompt is not a permission
  layer.
- Secrets stay in `.env` and the OS keyring. Never paste a key into a note, a commit, or
  a chat.

## Tools already connected

- **Firecrawl** — CLI + 28 skills. Prefer it over MCP; the hosted MCP server was removed
  on purpose (the key would sit in plaintext in `~/.Codex.json`).
- **Google Workspace** — `gws` CLI, GCP project `ai-os-joshua`. Gmail, Calendar, Drive,
  Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, People.
- **GitHub** — `gh` CLI, authenticated.

## Cost discipline

`AGENTS.md` reloads on every message, so keep this file lean. Prefer CLIs to MCP servers
(an MCP server can cost ~18k tokens per message in tool definitions). `/clear` between
unrelated tasks. Run the `handoff` skill past ~25% context rather than waiting for
auto-compact.

# Jay 2 — operating instructions for Codex (ai-os)

The canonical root is the repository directory containing this file (`C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os` on this Windows machine). Resolve paths from the repository root instead of assuming a saved Mac or Windows absolute path. This is the router: it holds pointers, not knowledge. Read it, then follow the routing map to the right file instead of searching blind. Twin for Claude Code: `CLAUDE.md`.

## Identity and mission

You are **Jay 2**, Joshua's executive assistant. This root is his EA workspace and command center. Joshua is the founder of Aspiring Attorneys and builder of LSAT U (lsatprep.study), a premium LSAT prep platform; he is the product, voice, and content authority. Your job: take operations, admin, drafting, and research off his plate so his time goes to teaching and building. Frame work as decisions and tradeoffs, not basics.

Standing duties, run from here without re-briefing: student operations (transcripts, assignments, follow-ups via `students/`), prospect and consultation correspondence (drafted in his voice, **never auto-sent unless a pre-approved template**), platform actions on lsatprep.study, session-note ingestion from Gmail/Drive, and keeping the wiki ledgers (`tasks`/`hot`/`log`) current so the next session starts oriented.

## Routing map

Paths are relative to the repository root.

| Need | Path |
|---|---|
| **Who Joshua is** (identity, preferences, contact) | `context/about-me.md` |
| **The business** (offers, money, channels, gaps) | `context/work.md` |
| **Current priorities** (the 90-day slate) | `context/priorities.md` |
| **What we decided and why** (locked decisions) | `decisions/log.md` |
| Freshest session state (hot cache) | `wiki/hot.md` |
| LLM Wiki schema (source, page, ingest/query/lint rules) | `system/schema/llm-wiki.md` |
| Master index · work ledger · dated history | `wiki/index.md` · `wiki/tasks.md` · `wiki/log.md` |
| Product ground truth (pointers to live backends) | `wiki/dashboard.md` |
| LSAT teaching knowledge | `corpus/index.md` |
| A student — profile, transcripts, work, correspondence | `students/<name>/` — start at `students/README.md` |
| Voice for anything a student or prospect reads | `wiki/teaching-voice.md` |
| Was it sent? (every outbound draft/send) | `wiki/send-ledger.md` — append-only; Gmail is authority |
| Who the students are (name, email, sessions, links) | `students/roster.generated.md` — regenerate, never hand-edit |
| Learned facts and preferences (automemory) | native store `~/.claude/projects/C--Users-Joshu-dev-ai-os/memory/` + `MEMORY.md` index |
| Skill / agent catalog | `skills/INDEX.md`, `agents/` |
| Systems Jay 2 can reach (registry) | `connections.md` — 7 data domains, mechanism/auth/freshness; read by `/audit` |
| Operator brain (how to think about automation) | `references/3ms-framework.md` — the Three Ms; walked weekly by `/level-up` |
| Automation build backlog (what to build next, ranked) | `references/automation-backlog.md` — corpus-derived gaps + tiers; feeds `/level-up` |
| How-it-works reference notes (methods, not state) | `references/` — also `references/claude-plus-codex.md`, `references/obsidian-command-center.md`, `references/second-brain-levels.md` |
| Web research and Firecrawl agents | `references/firecrawl.md` (guidelines in `references/firecrawl/`) |
| Immutable source evidence · intake queue | `raw/sources/` · `raw/inbox/` — one inbox, one archive |
| Archived web clips, with provenance + hashes | `raw/sources/clips/<slug>/` — clip + `PROVENANCE.md` + `SHA256SUMS` |
| Raw personal-data exports (Google Takeout, Gemini session transcripts) | `raw/data-about-me/` — unprocessed PII, git-ignored; never read wholesale |
| Design/plan thinking, dated (grill-me + interview outputs) | `brainstorms/` — supersedes the retired `aios/` reform folder |
| Session handoffs · chat exports | `handoffs/` — operational records, deliberately OUTSIDE `raw/`; `session-handoff` writes here |
| External teardowns and research, dated | `research/` |
| Web-clipped articles (Obsidian Web Clipper) | `raw/inbox/` — unprocessed only; `ingest` copies and hash-verifies them into `raw/sources/clips/`; processed originals stay until removal is authorized |
| Application code | `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/` — own repo, own instructions, own remote |
| Other projects (life-path, …) | `../ai-os-projects/<name>/` — each with its own `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/` |

Application repositories and dependencies stay outside this Obsidian vault, in sibling `../ai-os-projects/`. Do not create a junction from the vault back into that directory.

## Retrieval order

1. `wiki/hot.md` — current-session narrative and open threads.
2. `wiki/index.md` → the page (teaching knowledge: `corpus/index.md`; a student: their folder). Follow links; there is no semantic search and none is needed at this size.
3. The live system — the final freshness escalation.

**Live systems are authority for operational state; the brain mirrors them:** Cal.com + Google Calendar own sessions scheduled/used, LSAT U Supabase owns homework status/dossier/publish state, Stripe owns payment events, Gmail owns correspondence. On any disagreement, the backend wins. The brain is primary — nothing upstream holds them — for transcripts, teaching notes, judgments, prep briefs, curriculum, product specs, and decisions.

**Do not read the wiki unless the task needs it.** Retrieval costs context every turn. Skip it for: code edits in `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/`; shell/Git/file ops; questions the injected memories already answer; a skill run that names its own inputs; anything mechanical and self-contained. Route to it for: what is X · what did we decide and why · who a student is and where they stand · anything drafted in Joshua's voice for someone else · any decision touching roadmap, pedagogy, or UX.

**LLM Wiki schema:** For knowledge intake, knowledge questions, durable synthesis, and wiki maintenance, follow `system/schema/llm-wiki.md`. Use `ingest` as the single intake entry point; keep sources immutable, compile into existing pages, update the complete fenced catalog in `wiki/index.md`, and append changes to `wiki/log.md`. Preserve domain homes and live-system authority. Mechanical tasks retain the retrieval exceptions above.

**Wiki operations (LLM-wiki pattern):** the LLM writes/maintains `wiki/` and `corpus/`; Joshua sources, explores, asks. Raw sources are immutable — read, never modify. *Ingest:* read the source from `raw/`, discuss takeaways, write/update the pages it touches, update `wiki/index.md`, append to `wiki/log.md` (`## [YYYY-MM-DD] ingest | Title`); one source at a time, supervised, unless Joshua says batch. *Query:* index first, then pages; file valuable answers back as pages so explorations compound. *Lint:* `second-brain-lint` for contradictions, stale claims, orphans, missing pages.

## Voice

- **No em-dashes, ever.** Joshua never types them; a stray em-dash reads as AI and costs trust.
- **No AI-slop vocabulary** — never "delve," "tapestry," "testament," "demystify," "boasts," "in the realm of," and their kin.
- **Anything a student or prospect will read** routes through `wiki/teaching-voice.md` and is drafted, never sent, unless it is a pre-approved template.
- **LSAT teaching:** use project-owned `lsat-u-voice` and `references/lsat-teaching-voice-standard.md`; this Joshua-selected standard takes precedence over older vendor voice blends.
- **When an outbound message is authorized**, preserve the draft's paragraph breaks, list lines, and intentional spacing. After sending, compare the recipient-facing rendering with the draft and confirm exactly one copy landed. Report any mismatch; never resend automatically.
- **Lead with your recommendation, not a menu.** Be decisive; don't over-hedge.
- **Any prompt Joshua will paste elsewhere** goes inside a fenced code block, never inline prose.

## Tools, keys, and secrets

- **The entire secret model is `.env` + `.gitignore`.** The root `.env` (git-ignored — verify with `git check-ignore .env`) is Joshua's single central store for **everything**: API keys, passwords, and bank/account info (decided 2026-07-17). OAuth client secrets live in `~/.config/gws/`, outside the repo. There is no vault, no Keychain, no encrypted store (`records.sparsebundle` is dead) and none is wanted. - **95% rule.** Make no changes until you are 95% confident what Joshua wants. Ask until you are.
- **Lovable credits require confirmation.** Never take an action that spends or may spend Lovable credits without Joshua's explicit confirmation immediately before the action. - Begin at the Git-root `AGENTS.md` and follow directory-scoped instruction files toward the working path; the nearest file wins for its subtree.
- Keep root instructions inside the runtime byte budget. Move narrow rules to the narrowest owning directory rather than growing this file.

Sign-in uses email. Never report a UI change complete on the strength of the diff alone. This is the single biggest recurring failure across past sessions — a hard gate, not a suggestion.\\r\\n- **Responsive fixes carry a wider gate: verify across the full emulate matrix BEFORE pushing, not after Joshua reports it.** Narrow, mid, and wide viewports plus the sidecar-docked case, every time. A pushed \\"fix\\" that does not hold costs a second full session; this has already happened once.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Workflow Expectations\\r\\n\\r\\n- Run `npm run build` before wrapping up significant code or documentation work.\\r\\n- If tests are relevant to the change, run them too.\\r\\n- After completing a change, stage the intended files, commit with a concise message, and push to `origin main` unless the user says otherwise.\\r\\n- **Push via `.claude/safe-push.sh`, not raw `git push`.** Lovable auto-commits to `main` mid-session, so a raw push can be rejected or race a concurrent commit. The script fetches, merges `origin/main` if it diverged (never rebases, never force-pushes), then pushes. It also gates on `npm run typecheck`.\\r\\n- **Never roll `main` back.** Do not use Lovable\'s \\"Revert to commit\\", \\"revert and resend\\", or history restore, and never reset or force-push `main`. To undo your own work, `git revert <your SHA>` only. ## assistant

Intro to LR separates drill setup from the active exercise:

- `IntroDrillPage.tsx`: spacious title and summary, question count, Back, and Start Drill.
- `/drills/<slug>/run`: focused runner with a compact task heading, question counter, response controls, feedback, and Next.
- `ConclusionTypeLab.tsx`: separate stimulus and choices; feedback appears after submission. Its runner uses a 760px content width and 44px controls.

Use that structure for Conditional drills: specific instructions on the landing page, then a compact active view with Back to instructions. Keep Conditional content and formative state contracts.

Verified reference routes include `/bootcamp/intro-to-lr/drills/conclusion-type-lab` and its `/run` destination. No ungated Intro drill preview was found.

Leads to, will, and always can also express a definite result in a rule, but the word alone doesn\'t settle the meaning. “The studio will open tomorrow” gives us no sufficient condition to put on the left.</p>\\r\\n        <p>We\'ll now examine the Group 1 expressions individually. Keep asking what each sentence makes sufficient, rather than sorting words without their meaning.</p>\\r\\n      </> : <>\\r\\n        <p>A useful way to read the whole rule is: <strong>the left condition requires the right condition</strong>. Suppose borrowing a studio camera requires a current membership. What is required for borrowing? A current membership. That\'s the necessary condition.</p>\\r\\n        <div className=\\"co-word-comparison\\"><div><blockquote>Borrowing a studio camera requires a current membership.</blockquote><p>The required idea comes after requires. Find the whole idea: a current membership.</p></div><div><blockquote>A current membership is required to borrow a studio camera.</blockquote><p>The same required idea now comes first. Moving it in the sentence hasn\'t changed what borrowing requires.</p></div></div>\\r\\n        <Arrow left=\\"Borrows studio camera\\" right=\\"Has current membership\\"/>\\r\\n        <ThinkPause prompt=\\"Mina has a current membership. Does this rule tell us she borrowed a camera?\\">\\r\\n          <p>No. Membership is something borrowing requires. Mina could have the membership and never borrow a camera. Accessibility (A11y)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Check for**:\\r\\n- **Contrast issues**: Text contrast ratios < 4.5:1 (or 7:1 for AAA)\\r\\n- **Missing ARIA**: Interactive elements without proper roles, labels, or states\\r\\n- **Keyboard navigation**: Missing focus indicators, illogical tab order, keyboard traps\\r\\n- **Semantic HTML**: Improper heading hierarchy, missing landmarks, divs instead of buttons\\r\\n- **Alt text**: Missing or poor image descriptions\\r\\n- **Form issues**: Inputs without labels, poor error messaging, missing required indicators\\r\\n\\r\\n**Score 0-4**: 0=Inaccessible (fails WCAG A), 1=Major gaps (few ARIA labels, no keyboard nav), 2=Partial (some a11y effort, significant gaps), 3=Good (WCAG AA mostly met, minor gaps), 4=Excellent (WCAG AA fully met, approaches AAA)\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2. [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 1.9 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"2c400f","wall_time_seconds":0.6162079,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":2807,"output":"# Product register\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen design SERVES the product: app UIs, admin dashboards, settings panels, data tables, tools, authenticated surfaces, anything where the user is in a task.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The product slop test\\r\\n\\r\\nNot \\"would someone say AI made this\\" — familiarity is often a feature here. The test is: would a user fluent in the category\'s best tools (Linear, Figma, Notion, Raycast, Stripe come to mind) sit down and trust this interface, or pause at every subtly-off component?\\r\\n\\r\\nProduct UI\'s failure mode isn\'t flatness, it\'s strangeness without purpose: over-decorated buttons, mismatched form controls, gratuitous motion, display fonts where labels should be, invented affordances for standard tasks. The bar is earned familiarity. The tool should disappear into the task.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Typography\\r\\n\\r\\n- **System fonts are legitimate.** `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \\"Segoe UI\\", system-ui, sans-serif` gives you native feel on every platform. Inter is the common cross-platform default for a reason.\\r\\n- **One family is often right.** Product UIs don\'t need display/body pairing. A well-tuned sans carries headings, buttons, labels, body, data.\\r\\n- **Fixed rem scale, not fluid.** Clamp-sized headings don\'t serve product UI. Users view at consistent DPI, and a fluid h1 that shrinks in a sidebar looks worse, not better.\\r\\n- **Tighter scale ratio.** 1.125–1.2 between steps is typical. More type elements here than on brand surfaces; exaggerated contrast creates noise.\\r\\n- **Line length still applies for prose** (65–75ch). Data and compact UI can run denser — tables at 120ch+ are fine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Color\\r\\n\\r\\nProduct defaults to Restrained. A single surface can earn Committed — a dashboard where one category color carries a report, an onboarding flow with a drenched welcome screen — but Restrained is the floor.\\r\\n\\r\\n- State-rich semantic vocabulary: hover, focus, active, disabled, selected, loading, error, warning, success, info. Standardize these.\\r\\n- Accent color used for primary actions, current selection, and state indicators only — not decoration.\\r\\n- A second neutral layer for sidebars, toolbars, and panels (slightly cooler or warmer than the content surface).\\r\\n\\r\\n## Layout\\r\\n\\r\\n- Predictable grids. Consistency IS an affordance — users navigate faster when the structure is expected.\\r\\n- Familiar patterns are features. Standard navigation (top bar, side nav), breadcrumbs, tabs, and form layouts have established user expectations. Don\'t reinvent for flavor.\\r\\n- Responsive behavior is structural (collapse sidebar, responsive table, breakpoint-driven columns), not fluid typography.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Components\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery interactive component has: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error. Don\'t ship with half of these.\\r\\n\\r\\n- Skeleton states for loading, not spinners in the middle of content.\\r\\n- Empty states that teach the interface, not \\"nothing here.\\"\\r\\n- Consistent affordances across the surface. Same button shape. Same form-control vocabulary. Same icon style.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Motion\\r\\n\\r\\n- 150–250 ms on most transitions. Users are in flow — don\'t make them wait for choreography.\\r\\n- Motion conveys state, not decoration. State change, feedback, loading, reveal — nothing else.\\r\\n- No orchestrated page-load sequences. Product loads into a task; users don\'t want to watch it load.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Product bans (on top of the shared absolute bans)\\r\\n\\r\\n- Decorative motion that doesn\'t convey state.\\r\\n- Inconsistent component vocabulary across screens. If the \\"save\\" button looks different in two places, one is wrong.\\r\\n- Display fonts in UI labels, buttons, data.\\r\\n- Reinventing standard affordances for flavor (custom scrollbars, weird form controls, non-standard modals).\\r\\n- Heavy color or full-saturation accents on inactive states.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Product permissions\\r\\n\\r\\nProduct can afford things brand surfaces can\'t.\\r\\n\\r\\n- System fonts and familiar sans defaults (Inter, SF Pro, system-ui stacks).\\r\\n- Standard navigation patterns: top bar + side nav, breadcrumbs, tabs, command palettes.\\r\\n- Density. Tables with many rows, panels with many labels, dense information when users need it.\\r\\n- Consistency over surprise. The same visual vocabulary screen to screen is a virtue; delight is saved for moments, not pages.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: impeccable\\r\\ndescription: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, clarify, distill, harden, optimize, adapt, animate, colorize, extract, or otherwise improve a frontend interface. Covers websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, app shells, components, forms, settings, onboarding, and empty states. Handles UX review, visual hierarchy, information architecture, cognitive load, accessibility, performance, responsive behavior, theming, anti-patterns, typography, fonts, spacing, layout, alignment, color, motion, micro-interactions, UX copy, error states, edge cases, i18n, and reusable design systems or tokens. Also use for bland designs that need to become bolder or more delightful, loud designs that should become quieter, live browser iteration on UI elements, or ambitious visual effects that should feel technically extraordinary. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nDesigns and iterates production-grade frontend interfaces. Real working code, committed design choices, exceptional craft.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Setup (non-optional)\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore any design work or file edits, pass these gates. Skipping them produces generic output that ignores the project.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Gate | Required check | If fail |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| Context | The PRODUCT.md / DESIGN.md loader result is known from `node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/load-context.mjs`. | Run the loader before continuing. |\\r\\n| Product | PRODUCT.md exists and is not empty or placeholder (`[TODO]` markers, <200 chars). | Run `$impeccable teach`, refresh context, then resume. Never synthesize PRODUCT.md from the user\'s original prompt alone. |\\r\\n| Command | The matching command reference is loaded when a sub-command is used. | Load the reference before continuing. |\\r\\n| Craft | `$impeccable craft` has a user-confirmed shape brief for this task. `teach` / PRODUCT.md never counts as shape. | Run `$impeccable shape` and wait for explicit brief confirmation. |\\r\\n| Image | Required visual probes / mocks are generated or skipped with a reason. | Resolve the image-generation gate in `shape.md` or `craft.md` before code. |\\r\\n| Mutation | All active gates above pass. | Do not edit project files yet. |\\r\\n\\r\\nCodex-style agents must state this before editing files:\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nIMPECCABLE_PREFLIGHT: context=pass product=pass command_reference=pass shape=pass|not_required image_gate=pass|skipped:<reason> mutation=open\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nFor `$impeccable craft`, `shape=pass` is only valid after a separate user response approving the shape design brief, or when the user provided an already-confirmed brief in the request. Do not mark `shape=pass` after writing PRODUCT.md, summarizing assumptions, or drafting an unconfirmed brief yourself.\\r\\n\\r\\nOther harnesses should follow the same checklist when they can expose this state.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1. Context gathering\\r\\n\\r\\nTwo files, case-insensitive. The loader looks at the project root by default and falls back to `.agents/context/` and `docs/` if the root is clean. Override with `IMPECCABLE_CONTEXT_DIR=path/to/dir` (absolute or relative to cwd).\\r\\n\\r\\n- **PRODUCT.md** — required. Users, brand, tone, anti-references, strategic principles.\\r\\n- **DESIGN.md** — optional, strongly recommended. Colors, typography, elevation, components.\\r\\n\\r\\nLoad both in one call:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nnode .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/load-context.mjs\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nConsume the full JSON output. Never pipe through `head`, `tail`, `grep`, or `jq`. The output\'s `contextDir` field tells you where the files were resolved from.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the output is already in this session\'s conversation history, don\'t re-run. Exceptions requiring a fresh load: you just ran `$impeccable teach` or `$impeccable document` (they rewrite the files), or the user manually edited one.\\r\\n\\r\\n`$impeccable live` already warms context via `live.mjs` — if you\'ve run `live.mjs`, don\'t also run `load-context.mjs` this session.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf PRODUCT.md is missing, empty, or placeholder (`[TODO]` markers, <200 chars): run `$impeccable teach`, then resume the user\'s original task with the fresh context. If the original task was `$impeccable craft`, resume into `$impeccable shape` before any implementation work.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf DESIGN.md is missing: nudge once per session (*\\"Run `$impeccable document` for more on-brand output\\"*), then proceed.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2. Register\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery design task is **brand** (marketing, landing, campaign, long-form content, portfolio — design IS the product) or **product** (app UI, admin, dashboard, tool — design SERVES the product).\\r\\n\\r\\nIdentify before designing. Priority: (1) cue in the task itself (\\"landing page\\" vs \\"dashboard\\"); (2) the surface in focus (the page, file, or route being worked on); (3) `register` field in PRODUCT.md. First match wins.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf PRODUCT.md lacks the `register` field (legacy), infer it once from its \\"Users\\" and \\"Product Purpose\\" sections, then cache the inferred value for the session. Suggest the user run `$impeccable teach` to add the field explicitly.\\r\\n\\r\\nLoad the matching reference: [reference/brand.md](reference/brand.md) or [reference/product.md](reference/product.md). The shared design laws below apply to both.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Shared design laws\\r\\n\\r\\nApply to every design, both registers. Match implementation complexity to the aesthetic vision — maximalism needs elaborate code, minimalism needs precision. Interpret creatively. Vary across projects; never converge on the same choices. GPT is capable of extraordinary work — don\'t hold back.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Color\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use OKLCH. Reduce chroma as lightness approaches 0 or 100 — high chroma at extremes looks garish.\\r\\n- Never use `#000` or `#fff`. Tint every neutral toward the brand hue (chroma 0.005–0.01 is enough).\\r\\n- Pick a **color strategy** before picking colors. Four steps on the commitment axis:\\r\\n  - **Restrained** — tinted neutrals + one accent ≤10%. Product default; brand minimalism.\\r\\n  - **Committed** — one saturated color carries 30–60% of the surface. Brand default for identity-driven pages.\\r\\n  - **Full palette** — 3–4 named roles, each used deliberately. Brand campaigns; product data viz.\\r\\n  - **Drenched** — the surface IS the color. Brand heroes, campaign pages.\\r\\n- The \\"one accent ≤10%\\" rule is Restrained only. Committed / Full palette / Drenched exceed it on purpose. Don\'t collapse every design to Restrained by reflex.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Theme\\r\\n\\r\\nDark vs. light is never a default. Not dark \\"because tools look cool dark.\\" Not light \\"to be safe.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore choosing, write one sentence of physical scene: who uses this, where, under what ambient light, in what mood. If the sentence doesn\'t force the answer, it\'s not concrete enough — add detail until it does.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\"Observability dashboard\\" does not force an answer. \\"SRE glancing at incident severity on a 27-inch monitor at 2am in a dim room\\" does. Run the sentence, not the category.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Typography\\r\\n\\r\\n- Cap body line length at 65–75ch.\\r\\n- Hierarchy through scale + weight contrast (≥1.25 ratio between steps). (Not bold in one section, semibold in another for the same role)\\r\\n   - Is letter-spacing intentional or default everywhere?\\r\\n\\r\\n**CRITICAL**: The goal isn\'t to make text \\"fancier\\" — it\'s to make it clearer, more readable, and more intentional. Good typography is invisible; bad typography is distracting.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Plan Typography Improvements\\r\\n\\r\\nConsult the [typography reference](typography.md) for detailed guidance on scales, pairing, and loading strategies.\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a systematic plan:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Font selection**: Do fonts need replacing? What fits the brand/context?\\r\\n- **Type scale**: Establish a modular scale (e.g., 1.25 ratio) with clear hierarchy\\r\\n- **Weight strategy**: Which weights serve which roles? (Regular for body, Semibold for labels, Bold for headings — or whatever fits)\\r\\n- **Spacing**: Line-heights, letter-spacing, and margins between typographic elements\\r\\n\\r\\n## Improve Typography Systematically\\r\\n\\r\\n### Font Selection\\r\\n\\r\\nIf fonts need replacing:\\r\\n- Choose fonts that reflect the brand personality\\r\\n- Pair with genuine contrast (serif + sans, geometric + humanist) — or use a single family in multiple weights\\r\\n- Ensure web font loading doesn\'t cause layout shift (`font-display: swap`, metric-matched fallbacks)\\r\\n\\r\\n### Establish Hierarchy\\r\\n\\r\\nBuild a clear type scale:\\r\\n- **5 sizes cover most needs**: caption, secondary, body, subheading, heading\\r\\n- **Use a consistent ratio** between levels (1.25, 1.333, or 1.5)\\r\\n- **Combine dimensions**: Size + weight + color + space for strong hierarchy — don\'t rely on size alone\\r\\n- **App UIs**: Use a fixed `rem`-based type scale, optionally adjusted at 1-2 breakpoints. Fluid sizing undermines the spatial predictability that dense, container-based layouts need\\r\\n- **Marketing / content pages**: Use fluid sizing via `clamp(min, preferred, max)` for headings and display text. Keep body text fixed\\r\\n\\r\\n### Fix Readability\\r\\n\\r\\n- Set `max-width` on text containers using `ch` units (`max-width: 65ch`)\\r\\n- Adjust line-height per context: tighter for headings (1.1-1.2), looser for body (1.5-1.7)\\r\\n- Increase line-height slightly for light-on-dark text\\r\\n- Ensure body text is at least 16px / 1rem\\r\\n\\r\\n### Refine Details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use `tabular-nums` for data tables and numbers that should align\\r\\n- Apply proper `letter-spacing`: slightly open for small caps and uppercase, default or tight for large display text\\r\\n- Use semantic token names (`--text-body`, `--text-heading`), not value names (`--font-16`)\\r\\n- Set `font-kerning: normal` and consider OpenType features where appropriate\\r\\n\\r\\n### Weight Consistency\\r\\n\\r\\n- Define clear roles for each weight and stick to them\\r\\n- Don\'t use more than 3-4 weights (Regular, Medium, Semibold, Bold is plenty)\\r\\n- Load only the weights you actually use (each weight adds to page load)\\r\\n\\r\\n**NEVER**:\\r\\n- Use more than 2-3 font families\\r\\n- Pick sizes arbitrarily — commit to a scale\\r\\n- Set body text below 16px\\r\\n- Use decorative/display fonts for body text\\r\\n- Disable browser zoom (`user-scalable=no`)\\r\\n- Use `px` for font sizes — use `rem` to respect user settings\\r\\n- Default to Inter/Roboto/Open Sans when personality matters\\r\\n- Pair fonts that are similar but not identical (two geometric sans-serifs)\\r\\n\\r\\n## Verify Typography Improvements\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Hierarchy**: Can you identify heading vs body vs caption instantly?\\r\\n- **Readability**: Is body text comfortable to read in long passages?\\r\\n- **Consistency**: Are same-role elements styled identically throughout?\\r\\n- **Personality**: Does the typography reflect the brand?\\r\\n- **Performance**: Are web fonts loading efficiently without layout shift?\\r\\n- **Accessibility**: Does text meet WCAG contrast ratios? Is it zoomable to 200%?\\r\\n\\r\\nRemember: Typography is the foundation of interface design — it carries the majority of information. Getting it right is the highest-leverage improvement you can make.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Live-mode signature params\\r\\n\\r\\nEach variant MUST declare a `scale` param controlling the hierarchy ratio. Express all font sizes in the variant\'s scoped CSS through `calc(var(--p-scale, 1) * <base>)` or, better, scale the type ramp via `clamp(min, calc(var(--p-scale, 1) * Npx), max)`. Users slide from subdued to commanding.\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\"id\\":\\"scale\\",\\"kind\\":\\"range\\",\\"min\\":0.85,\\"max\\":1.3,\\"step\\":0.05,\\"default\\":1,\\"label\\":\\"Scale\\"}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWhere the variant riffs on a specific pairing, expose the pairing choice as a `steps` param (e.g. \\"serif display + sans body\\" vs. \\"mono display + sans body\\" vs. \\"all-sans\\"). Each branch routes through `:scope[data-p-pairing=\\"X\\"]` selectors in scoped CSS.\\r\\n\\r\\nSee `reference/live.md` for the full params contract.\\r\\nAssess and improve layout and spacing that feels monotonous, crowded, or structurally weak — turning generic arrangements into intentional, rhythmic compositions.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Register\\r\\n\\r\\nBrand: asymmetric compositions, fluid spacing with `clamp()`, intentional grid-breaking for emphasis. Rhythm through contrast — tight groupings paired with generous separations.\\r\\n\\r\\nProduct: predictable grids, consistent densities, familiar navigation patterns. Responsive behavior is structural (collapse sidebar, responsive table), not fluid typography. Consistency IS an affordance.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Assess Current Layout\\r\\n\\r\\nAnalyze what\'s weak about the current spatial design:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Spacing**:\\r\\n   - Is spacing consistent or arbitrary? (Random padding/margin values)\\r\\n   - Is all spacing the same? (Equal padding everywhere = no rhythm)\\r\\n   - Are related elements grouped tightly, with generous space between groups?\\r\\n\\r\\n2. **Visual hierarchy**:\\r\\n   - Apply the squint test: blur your (metaphorical) eyes — can you still identify the most important element, second most important, and clear groupings?\\r\\n   - Is hierarchy achieved effectively? (Space and weight alone can be enough — but is the current approach working?)\\r\\n   - Does whitespace guide the eye to what matters?\\r\\n\\r\\n3. **Grid & structure**:\\r\\n   - Is there a clear underlying structure, or does the layout feel random?\\r\\n   - Are identical card grids used everywhere? (Icon + heading + text, repeated endlessly)\\r\\n   - Is everything centered? (Left-aligned with asymmetric layouts feels more designed, but not a hard and fast rule)\\r\\n\\r\\n4. **Rhythm & variety**:\\r\\n   - Does the layout have visual rhythm? (Alternating tight/generous spacing)\\r\\n   - Is every section structured the same way? (Monotonous repetition)\\r\\n   - Are there intentional moments of surprise or emphasis?\\r\\n\\r\\n5. **Density**:\\r\\n   - Is the layout too cramped? (Not enough breathing room)\\r\\n   - Is the layout too sparse? (Excessive whitespace without purpose)\\r\\n   - Does density match the content type? (Data-dense UIs need tighter spacing; marketing pages need more air)\\r\\n\\r\\n**CRITICAL**: Layout problems are often the root cause of interfaces feeling \\"off\\" even when colors and fonts are fine. Space is a design material — use it with intention.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Plan Layout Improvements\\r\\n\\r\\nConsult the [spatial design reference](spatial-design.md) for detailed guidance on grids, rhythm, and container queries.\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a systematic plan:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Spacing system**: Use a consistent scale — whether that\'s a framework\'s built-in scale (e.g., Tailwind), rem-based tokens, or a custom system. The specific values matter less than consistency.\\r\\n- **Hierarchy strategy**: How will space communicate importance?\\r\\n- **Layout approach**: What structure fits the content? Flex for 1D, Grid for 2D, named areas for complex page layouts.\\r\\n- **Rhythm**: Where should spacing be tight vs generous?\\r\\n\\r\\n## Improve Layout Systematically\\r\\n\\r\\n### Establish a Spacing System\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use a consistent spacing scale — framework scales (Tailwind, etc.), rem-based tokens, or a custom scale all work. What matters is that values come from a defined set, not arbitrary numbers.\\r\\n- Name tokens semantically if using custom properties: `--space-xs` through `--space-xl`, not `--spacing-8`\\r\\n- Use `gap` for sibling spacing instead of margins — eliminates margin collapse hacks\\r\\n- Apply `clamp()` for fluid spacing that breathes on larger screens\\r\\n\\r\\n### Create Visual Rhythm\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Tight grouping** for related elements (8-12px between siblings)\\r\\n- **Generous separation** between distinct sections (48-96px)\\r\\n- **Varied spacing** within sections — not every row needs the same gap\\r\\n- **Asymmetric compositions** — break the predictable centered-content pattern when it makes sense\\r\\n\\r\\n### Choose the Right Layout Tool\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Use Flexbox for 1D layouts**: Rows of items, nav bars, button groups, card contents, most component internals. Flex is simpler and more appropriate for the majority of layout tasks.\\r\\n- **Use Grid for 2D layouts**: Page-level structure, dashboards, data-dense interfaces, anything where rows AND columns need coordinated control.\\r\\n- **Don\'t default to Grid** when Flexbox with `flex-wrap` would be simpler and more flexible.\\r\\n- Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))` for responsive grids without breakpoints.\\r\\n- Use named grid areas (`grid-template-areas`) for complex page layouts — redefine at breakpoints.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Break Card Grid Monotony\\r\\n\\r\\n- Don\'t default to card grids for everything — spacing and alignment create visual grouping naturally\\r\\n- Use cards only when content is truly distinct and actionable — never nest cards inside cards\\r\\n- Vary card sizes, span columns, or mix cards with non-card content to break repetition\\r\\n\\r\\n### Strengthen Visual Hierarchy\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use the fewest dimensions needed for clear hierarchy. Space alone can be enough — generous whitespace around an element draws the eye. Some of the most sophisticated designs achieve rhythm with just space and weight. Add color or size contrast only when simpler means aren\'t sufficient.\\r\\n- Be aware of reading flow — in LTR languages, the eye naturally scans top-left to bottom-right, but primary action placement depends on context (e.g., bottom-right in dialogs, top in navigation).\\r\\n- Create clear content groupings through proximity and separation.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Manage Depth & Elevation\\r\\n\\r\\n- Create a semantic z-index scale (dropdown → sticky → modal-backdrop → modal → toast → tooltip)\\r\\n- Build a consistent shadow scale (sm → md → lg → xl) — shadows should be subtle\\r\\n- Use elevation to reinforce hierarchy, not as decoration\\r\\n\\r\\n### Optical Adjustments\\r\\n\\r\\n- If an icon looks visually off-center despite being geometrically centered, nudge it — but only if you\'re confident it actually looks wrong. Don\'t adjust speculatively.\\r\\n\\r\\n**NEVER**:\\r\\n- Use arbitrary spacing values outside your scale\\r\\n- Make all spacing equal — variety creates hierarchy\\r\\n- Wrap everything in cards — not everything needs a container\\r\\n- Nest cards inside cards — use spacing and dividers for hierarchy within\\r\\n- Use identical card grids everywhere (icon + heading + text, repeated)\\r\\n- Center everything — left-aligned with asymmetry feels more designed\\r\\n- Default to the hero metric layout (big number, small label, stats, gradient) as a template. If showing real user data, a prominent metric can work — but it should display actual data, not decorative numbers.\\r\\n- Default to CSS Grid when Flexbox would be simpler — use the simplest tool for the job\\r\\n- Use arbitrary z-index values (999, 9999) — build a semantic scale\\r\\n\\r\\n## Verify Layout Improvements\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Squint test**: Can you identify primary, secondary, and groupings with blurred vision?\\r\\n- **Rhythm**: Does the page have a satisfying beat of tight and generous spacing?\\r\\n- **Hierarchy**: Is the most important content obvious within 2 seconds?\\r\\n- **Breathing room**: Does the layout feel comfortable, not cramped or wasteful?\\r\\n- **Consistency**: Is the spacing system applied uniformly?\\r\\n- **Responsiveness**: Does the layout adapt gracefully across screen sizes?\\r\\n\\r\\nRemember: Space is the most underused design tool. A layout with the right rhythm and hierarchy can make even simple content feel polished and intentional.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Live-mode signature params\\r\\n\\r\\nEach variant MUST declare a `density` param. Drive all spacing tokens in the variant\'s scoped CSS through `calc(var(--p-density, 1) * <base>)` — paddings, gaps, column widths. Users slide from airy to packed and see layout re-breathe with no regeneration.\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\"id\\":\\"density\\",\\"kind\\":\\"range\\",\\"min\\":0.6,\\"max\\":1.4,\\"step\\":0.05,\\"default\\":1,\\"label\\":\\"Density\\"}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nFor variants whose topology genuinely changes (stacked vs. side-by-side, grid vs. bento), use a `steps` param whose scoped CSS branches via `:scope[data-p-structure=\\"X\\"]`. One structure param + one density param is a powerful combo; resist adding a third.\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\"id\\":\\"structure\\",\\"kind\\":\\"steps\\",\\"default\\":\\"grid\\",\\"label\\":\\"Structure\\",\\"options\\":[\\r\\n  {\\"value\\":\\"stacked\\",\\"label\\":\\"Stacked\\"},\\r\\n  {\\"value\\":\\"grid\\",\\"label\\":\\"Grid\\"},\\r\\n  {\\"value\\":\\"bento\\",\\"label\\":\\"Bento\\"}\\r\\n]}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nSee `reference/live.md` for the full params contract.\\r\\n> **Additional context needed**: target platforms/devices and usage contexts.\\r\\n\\r\\nAdapt existing designs to work effectively across different contexts - different screen sizes, devices, platforms, or use cases.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Assess Adaptation Challenge\\r\\n\\r\\nUnderstand what needs adaptation and why:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Identify the source context**:\\r\\n   - What was it designed for originally? (Desktop web? Mobile app?)\\r\\n   - What assumptions were made? (Large screen? Mouse input? Fast connection?)\\r\\n   - What works well in current context?\\r\\n\\r\\n2. **Understand target context**:\\r\\n   - **Device**: Mobile, tablet, desktop, TV, watch, print?\\r\\n   - **Input method**: Touch, mouse, keyboard, voice, gamepad?\\r\\n   - **Screen constraints**: Size, resolution, orientation?\\r\\n   - **Connection**: Fast wifi, slow 3G, offline?\\r\\n   - **Usage context**: On-the-go vs desk, quick glance vs focused reading?\\r\\n   - **User expectations**: What do users expect on this platform?\\r\\n\\r\\n3. **Identify adaptation challenges**:\\r\\n   - What won\'t fit? (Content, navigation, features)\\r\\n   - What won\'t work? (Hover states on touch, tiny touch targets)\\r\\n   - What\'s inappropriate? (Desktop patterns on mobile, mobile patterns on desktop)\\r\\n\\r\\n**CRITICAL**: Adaptation is not just scaling - it\'s rethinking the experience for the new context.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Plan Adaptation Strategy\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate context-appropriate strategy:\\r\\n\\r\\n### Mobile Adaptation (Desktop → Mobile)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Layout Strategy**:\\r\\n- Single column instead of multi-column\\r\\n- Vertical stacking instead of side-by-side\\r\\n- Full-width components instead of fixed widths\\r\\n- Bottom navigation instead of top/side navigation\\r\\n\\r\\n**Interaction Strategy**:\\r\\n- Touch targets 44x44px minimum (not hover-dependent)\\r\\n- Swipe gestures where appropriate (lists, carousels)\\r\\n- Bottom sheets instead of dropdowns\\r\\n- Thumbs-first design (controls within thumb reach)\\r\\n- Larger tap areas with more spacing\\r\\n\\r\\n**Content Strategy**:\\r\\n- Progressive disclosure (don\'t show everything at once)\\r\\n- Prioritize primary content (secondary content in tabs/accordions)\\r\\n- Shorter text (more concise)\\r\\n- Larger text (16px minimum)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Navigation Strategy**:\\r\\n- Hamburger menu or bottom navigation\\r\\n- Reduce navigation complexity\\r\\n- Sticky headers for context\\r\\n- Back button in navigation flow\\r\\n\\r\\n### Tablet Adaptation (Hybrid Approach)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Layout Strategy**:\\r\\n- Two-column layouts (not single or three-column)\\r\\n- Side panels for secondary content\\r\\n- Master-detail views (list + detail)\\r\\n- Adaptive based on orientation (portrait vs landscape)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Interaction Strategy**:\\r\\n- Support both touch and pointer\\r\\n- Touch targets 44x44px but allow denser layouts than phone\\r\\n- Side navigation drawers\\r\\n- Multi-column forms where appropriate\\r\\n\\r\\n### Desktop Adaptation (Mobile → Desktop)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Layout Strategy**:\\r\\n- Multi-column layouts (use horizontal space)\\r\\n- Side navigation always visible\\r\\n- Multiple information panels simultaneously\\r\\n- Fixed widths with max-width constraints (don\'t stretch to 4K)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Interaction Strategy**:\\r\\n- Hover states for additional information\\r\\n- Keyboard shortcuts\\r\\n- Right-click context menus\\r\\n- Drag and drop where helpful\\r\\n- Multi-select with Shift/Cmd\\r\\n\\r\\n**Content Strategy**:\\r\\n- Show more information upfront (less progressive disclosure)\\r\\n- Data tables with many columns\\r\\n- Richer visualizations\\r\\n- More detailed descriptions\\r\\n\\r\\n### Print Adaptation (Screen → Print)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Layout Strategy**:\\r\\n- Page breaks at logical points\\r\\n- Remove navigation, footer, interactive elements\\r\\n- Black and white (or limited color)\\r\\n- Proper margins for binding\\r\\n\\r\\n**Content Strategy**:\\r\\n- Expand shortened content (show full URLs, hidden sections)\\r\\n- Add page numbers, headers, footers\\r\\n- Include metadata (print date, page title)\\r\\n- Convert charts to print-friendly versions\\r\\n\\r\\n### Email Adaptation (Web → Email)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Layout Strategy**:\\r\\n- Narrow width (600px max)\\r\\n- Single column only\\r\\n- Inline CSS (no external stylesheets)\\r\\n- Table-based layouts (for email client compatibility)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Interaction Strategy**:\\r\\n- Large, obvious CTAs (buttons not text links)\\r\\n- No hover states (not reliable)\\r\\n- Deep links to web app for complex interactions\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implement Adaptations\\r\\n\\r\\nApply changes systematically:\\r\\n\\r\\n### Responsive Breakpoints\\r\\n\\r\\nChoose appropriate breakpoints:\\r\\n- Mobile: 320px-767px\\r\\n- Tablet: 768px-102…945 tokens truncated…rd focus are present. Course category labels fail text contrast. |\\r\\n| Performance | 3/4 | No observed runtime errors or verified rendering defect in the walkthrough. Visited questions remain mounted to preserve work. No controlled load/frame benchmark was performed. |\\r\\n| Responsive design | 3/4 | Core exercise UI reflows at 320px and 768px. The drawer close target is only 16px square. |\\r\\n| Theming | 2/4 | The runner uses shared course tokens, but the course shell mixes them with literal colors. Light mode was verified; dark-mode integration was not. |\\r\\n| Anti-patterns | 2/4 | Nested containers and mechanical copy remain, particularly in independent writing. |\\r\\n| **Total** | **13/20** | **Acceptable: significant refinement remains.** |\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is an Impeccable rubric score, not a price, certification, or measured learning outcome.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Six issues, ordered by impact\\r\\n\\r\\nSeverity totals: **P0: 0 · P1: 1 · P2: 5 · P3: 0.**\\r\\n\\r\\n### [P1] Course category labels are too faint\\r\\n\\r\\n**Location:** [opening-course.css:5](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/opening-course.css:5), [opening-course.css:16](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/opening-course.css:16), and the previous/next captions at line 37.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Category:** Accessibility.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Verified evidence:** The 10px Practice eyebrow computes to `rgba(26,26,26,0.46)` over `rgb(245,242,237)`, approximately **2.90:1** after alpha compositing. Intro path, Practice and Tools in the rail use approximately **3.26:1**. These are visible informational labels, not disabled controls.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Impact:** Readers with reduced contrast sensitivity may miss the categories and navigation context. The small uppercase typography compounds the faint appearance.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Standard:** Normal text needs at least 4.5:1 under [WCAG 1.4.3, Contrast Minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html).\\r\\n\\r\\n**Recommendation:** Use a course muted-text token that clears 4.5:1 on the actual background. Apply it to the eyebrow, drawer/rail category labels and lesson navigation captions. Re-measure composited colors rather than judging a screenshot.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Suggested command:** `$impeccable harden`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### [P2] A completed practice session disappears on reload without a clear notice\\r\\n\\r\\n**Location:** [OpeningMixedDrill.tsx:74](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/OpeningMixedDrill.tsx:74), [MixedFamilyPractice.tsx:92](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/MixedFamilyPractice.tsx:92), and [routes.tsx:202](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/routes.tsx:202).\\r\\n\\r\\n**Category:** Interaction hardening / clarity.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Verified evidence:** After finishing 24 questions and a fresh check, Review my answers retained the selected answer and feedback. Reloading the separate audit tab returned to the first stage introduction. Questions, results and written drafts live in React state. The authenticated shell additionally has a global Saved to your account status, while the opening route supplies no persistence callbacks to this runner. That authenticated chrome was source-inspected, not browser-verified under a logged-in account.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Impact:** A student can lose substantial work and mistake the account saving status for a promise that this practice is saved.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Standard:** No WCAG violation asserted. This is a mismatch between saving scope and likely user expectations.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Recommendation:** Make the session-only scope explicit before starting and scope the authenticated saving status to the work it actually saves. If resumable practice is desired, define its persistence contract before connecting it to course progress. A local clarity fix does not require inventing a backend record.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Suggested commands:** `$impeccable clarify`, then `$impeccable harden` if persistence is added.\\r\\n\\r\\n### [P2] Review practice can open more questions\\r\\n\\r\\n**Location:** [OpeningMixedDrill.tsx:106](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/OpeningMixedDrill.tsx:106) and [OpeningMixedDrill.tsx:146](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/OpeningMixedDrill.tsx:146).\\r\\n\\r\\n**Category:** UX copy / interaction clarity.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Verified evidence:** One deliberately incorrect first answer created a qualification follow-up. At question 24, clicking Review practice opened Try the distinction in a new case and then another question, rather than the review.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Impact:** The action promises completion/review while asking the student to continue practicing. It makes a useful adaptive feature feel like an unexpected extension.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Standard:** No WCAG violation asserted.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Recommendation:** Use Try a fresh case when follow-ups are pending and Review practice when the next screen is the review. Share the branch decision between label and action so they cannot drift.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Suggested command:** `$impeccable clarify`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### [P2] Independent writing loses the shared exercise hierarchy\\r\\n\\r\\n**Location:** [MixedFamilyPractice.tsx:108](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/MixedFamilyPractice.tsx:108), [opening-mixed-drill.css:24](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/opening-mixed-drill.css:24), and the shared wrappers at [OpeningCourse.tsx:121](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/OpeningCourse.tsx:121).\\r\\n\\r\\n**Category:** Anti-patterns / typography / theming consistency.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Verified evidence:** Choice-question sentences render at 28px on desktop and 23px at 320px. The independent-writing sentence renders at **14px**, even on desktop. Its `co-lab co-check` container also adds an inner rounded panel inside the outer course panel. After comparison, the diagram and feedback introduce further enclosed surfaces.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Impact:** The sentence being tested becomes less prominent than instructions and fields. The stage looks like an embedded older component rather than the next part of one drill. Extra containers consume attention and mobile space.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Standard:** Impeccable\'s shared hierarchy and nested-card guidance. No WCAG failure is asserted solely from a 14px font.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Recommendation:** Give every stage a shared sentence treatment, instruction spacing, field spacing and feedback treatment. Use one exercise surface with internal spacing and dividers. Keep answer-input borders because they identify real controls. Consolidate course colors into scoped semantic tokens; do not assume the app\'s global dark mode already themes this light course shell.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Suggested commands:** `$impeccable typeset`, then `$impeccable layout`.\\r\\n\\r\\n![Independent writing: the tested sentence loses prominence inside nested panels](C:/Users/Joshu/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/07/01a117ea-7c95-7813-af3b-866b05ec963a/conditional-audit-written-stage.jpg)\\r\\n\\r\\n### [P2] Mobile menu controls do not consistently meet the 44px target\\r\\n\\r\\n**Location:** [sheet.tsx:60](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/components/ui/sheet.tsx:60), [OpeningCourse.tsx:25](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/OpeningCourse.tsx:25), [opening-course.css:99](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/components/opening-course.css:99).\\r\\n\\r\\n**Category:** Responsive design / accessibility usability.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Verified evidence:** At 320px, the drawer Close button measures **16 × 16px**. The Conditional logic link is **27.2px** high. The exercise buttons and Course menu trigger are at least 44px high. Close has an accessible name and visible keyboard ring; Escape closes the drawer.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Impact:** Closing the drawer is unnecessarily precise on a touch screen, despite good keyboard behavior.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Standard:** The Impeccable 44px target and [WCAG 2.5.5, Target Size Enhanced](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-enhanced.html).
